title: October 22 research · the October 30 option decision
conclusion: If forced to choose a target, Hinds 110 is the conditional first choice for a cheap, long-duration assignable option. No reviewed site is currently cleared for payment.
conditionalChoice: Hinds wins on disclosed land basis and the possibility that founder-reported power/fiber work can be documented quickly. Its ranking is not a finding that it is the most buildable site or has a known success probability.
counterargument: Texas permitting is a real current blocker. If Hinds cannot provide issuer documents and affordable extensions, Dillon 53 becomes the next negotiation target; New Castle follows. No automatic fallback purchase.

requirements.primary: 20–30 MW initial facility load; 25 MW working case, possible 50 MW expansion. Remote AI/HPC or centralized inference, low-water cooling and two constructible fiber routes. Energization window must be supplied by a buyer.
requirements.smallSite: 5–10 MW cases are a separate buyer-discovery hypothesis, not permission to relax land, network or power gates. Compute MW is not facility MW.
requirements.status: Unvalidated hypotheses; no named buyer has accepted any reviewed site.

capital.policyNote: Retain 52 factors, 16 proofs, conservative score >=70 and evidence confidence >=85. September 23 control-first G11 amendment remains explicitly proposed. Scores and success probability are not computed from missing evidence.

candidates.name: Hinds 110 / FM 2072
candidates.signal: Lowest disclosed land basis among the leading full-size candidates, plus founder-reported power/fiber progress. Best hypothesis for cheap, long-duration control.
candidates.risk: Exact 110-acre severance, utility/carrier writing, seller financing and assignment terms remain unresolved. TCEQ permit notice still blocks a dependable construction schedule.
candidates.nextTest: Obtain offered survey and the actual power/fiber letters; establish supplier, grid, MW, date, cost and transfer rights. Seek a low-fee, long option only after money gates clear.
candidates.priceNote: $319,000 MLS versus $319,500 Land.com. Reconcile with broker; approximately $2,900/advertised acre.
candidates.power: Founder says power and fiber are deliverable. Preserve that information; the underlying issuer documents have not been recovered. 138/345 kV crossings are marketing, not allocated MW.

candidates.name: Dillon-Baker compartment 53
candidates.signal: Traceable 60-acre tract, published ask and industrial/logistics context; no Texas permit-pause exposure.
candidates.risk: County RU use path, exact serving utility and load capacity remain open. Earlier screen found a narrow layout and drainage constraints.

candidates.power: No current exact-load service commitment recovered.

candidates.power: No current exact-load service commitment recovered.

candidates.name: Chiefland / Sherrill property

candidates.power: No current exact-load service commitment recovered.

candidates.power: No current exact-load service commitment recovered.

terms: Target $1,000 for six months, only after applicable payment gates pass; a negotiation target, not an accepted offer.
Two unilateral six-month extensions at no more than $1,000 each; total potential control 18 months. Seek a defined permit-delay extension/tolling provision, subject to a longstop.
Negotiate at or below the reconciled current asking price, attached to the exact 110-acre survey and legal description.
Counsel-approved assignment / nomination to a project buyer or affiliate, with no discretionary seller veto or surprise fee; utility/queue transfer is a separate approval.
Must be agreed now as the exercise purchase method: down payment, rate, amortization, balloon, security, recourse, prepayment and assignee assumption. No assumption the seller has accepted.
Owner authorization for utility, carrier, planning and title inquiries; controlled testing rights, data sharing, consultant reliance and seller cooperation.
No unconditional purchase obligation, automatic paid renewal or personal utility guarantee. Title/survey cures, cancellation and capped restoration obligations reviewed by Texas counsel.

Illustrative ceiling: $3,000 total option/extension fees + $2,000 legal/title + $3,000 scoped fatal screens + $2,000 contingency = $10,000. Include prior spend and commitments first; actual quotes may make this infeasible.

actions.title: Get the actual Hinds evidence pack
actions.channel: Founder call or listing inquiry; draft only
actions.question: I am evaluating Hinds 110 for phased computing use, with no committed tenant or capacity reservation. Please send the exact 110-acre survey/legal description, seller authority, easements, and every utility/carrier letter supporting the reported power and fiber. Please identify issuer, applicant, MW, delivery point/date, upgrade costs and transfer conditions. Would the seller discuss a low-fee assignable option with enforceable extensions and seller financing fixed in advance?
actions.decision: If no documents exist, power/fiber stay unverified and payment stays on hold.
actions.voicemail: William with Syncranicity, calling about Hinds 110. I need the offered survey and existing power/fiber letters before discussing conditional option terms. Please return my call.
actions.success: Exact offered survey plus dated issuer documents and named authorized seller.
actions.partial: Documents promised with owner and delivery date; no inferred gate pass.
actions.stop: No offered tract definition or demand for hard money before evidence.

actions.title: Resolve the actual utility and permit route
actions.contact: Serving utility named in seller documents; TCEQ Stormwater Permits Team
actions.channel: Utility channel remains unverified; SWGP@tceq.texas.gov verified on current official page
actions.question: For the exact offered tract and a genuine 20–30 MW facility phase / 50 MW expansion hypothesis, please identify DSP, TSP, ISO, intake steps, delivery point, schedule, upgrades, deposits, credit and transfer conditions. For TCEQ: which construction, generator and water authorizations would this design require, and what can proceed while the directive remains? Do not submit a funded application.

actions.voicemail: I am seeking the correct exact-parcel large-load intake and a written process, not a capacity reservation.
actions.success: Written exact-site process and credible scope-specific path with costs/dependencies.
actions.partial: Correct named desk plus document request; availability remains unknown.
actions.stop: No affordable studyable path or control cannot outlast the required milestone.

actions.title: Test whether a developer would pay for this position
actions.contact: Crusoe infrastructure/site-selection function; route through official contact page
actions.question: Your October 21 modular announcement prompted a requirements question. Would a remote North Texas site with a documented 20–30 MW facility phase and 50 MW path fit any acquisition program? What power cost/date, network latency, diversity, control term and evidence milestone would cause your team to consider paying for a transferable land position? We have no validated MW allocation or buyer-ready claim.
actions.decision: A modular product proves neither demand for Hinds nor willingness to pay an assignment premium.
actions.voicemail: William with Syncranicity. I would like the infrastructure site-selection contact for a requirements discussion before presenting a specific land opportunity.
actions.success: Dated requirement card from a relevant decision-maker and explicit evidence/payment hurdle.
actions.stop: Remote geography or scale rejected; retarget before commissioning reports.

actions.question: Please provide existing utility and county RU-use correspondence, offered surveys and easement schedules for compartments 53 and 48. Which tract can support a 20–25 MW layout, and would the owner entertain assignable, extendable low-fee control?
actions.decision: Dillon moves ahead only if its issuer evidence and control terms exceed Hinds, not merely because Texas is paused.
actions.voicemail: Calling about Baker compartments 53 and 48. Please share existing power, use and survey documents so we can compare layouts before discussing control.

decisionRule: By October 28, require the offered survey, seller authority, actual utility/carrier documents, a written permitting path, accepted economic terms and a takeout route meeting the operative policy. If they remain absent, do not pay on October 30. No fallback is pre-cleared.
texasContext: TCEQ continues to post its data-center permitting pause, including construction stormwater; October 19 was an agency-response deadline, not a promised restart. Rule 16 TAC 25.194 took effect October 8 for qualifying ERCOT large-load arrangements (including the defined co-location cases). Its $100,000 study fee and $50,000/MW intermediate security are not a fee quote for Hinds. A qualifying 75 MW case would imply $3.75 million of that security. Actual supplier, grid, load definition and applicability must be established first. SPP service would not remove statewide TCEQ requirements.
